title: Disaster Recovery for Data: RPO, RTO & Backup Strategy

scenes.heading: Disaster Recovery
scenes.narration: Disaster recovery is your plan for the worst day, and RPO and RTO are the two numbers that define how much loss and downtime you can accept.

scenes.heading: RPO vs RTO

left.title: RPO
points: How much data you can lose

right.title: RTO
points: How long to get back up

scenes.narration: The recovery point objective is how much data you can afford to lose, measured backward from the moment of failure, and it is governed by how often you back up. The recovery time objective is how long you can be down before service must return, and it is governed by how fast you can restore. Tightening either one costs money, so both are business decisions, not just technical ones.

scenes.heading: Backup strategy pillars
bullets: Follow the 3-2-1 rule: three copies, two media, one offsite
Match backup frequency to your RPO
Test restores regularly, not just backups
Protect backups from ransomware with immutability
scenes.narration: The classic three-two-one rule keeps three copies on two kinds of media with one copy offsite. Your backup frequency must be at least as tight as your recovery point objective, or the objective is fiction. Crucially, you must test restores regularly, because an untested backup is only a hope, and immutable backups protect you when ransomware tries to encrypt everything.

scenes.heading: The recovery drill
scenes.narration: A recovery drill begins with formally declaring a disaster so everyone shifts into recovery mode. You fail over to a backup region and restore from the most recent good backup. Then you validate data integrity before cutting production traffic back over, so you never resume on corrupted state.

scenes.heading: An RPO compliance check
scenes.code:
-- Alert if the newest backup is older than the RPO
SELECT
  MAX(backup_completed_at) AS latest_backup,
  NOW() - MAX(backup_completed_at) AS backup_age,
  CASE
    WHEN NOW() - MAX(backup_completed_at) > INTERVAL '15 minutes'
      THEN 'RPO_BREACH'
    ELSE 'OK'
  END AS rpo_status
FROM backup_catalog
WHERE dataset = 'orders';
scenes.narration: This check finds the most recent successful backup and compares its age against the recovery point objective. If the newest backup is older than fifteen minutes, the status flips to a breach and should page. Monitoring the objective continuously means you discover a lapsed backup before a disaster, not during one.

scenes.text: A backup you've never restored is not a backup — it's a hope. Test recovery on a schedule, and let RPO and RTO drive the design.
scenes.narration: A backup you have never actually restored is not a backup but a hope, so test recovery on a schedule and let your recovery point and time objectives drive the entire design.
